brief: Daily market wrap. S&P +66bps to 7774 (+13.6% ytd) on light volume, Nasdaq at a fresh high, semis up five weeks despite an 11% SOX pullback versus SPX +4% over two months, which GS reads as a more constructive setup into earnings than its cautious 2Q call. 10yr 5.32%, Brent $101, gold lower on higher yields and dollar, Bitcoin $85.5k, and Brazil's election has Bolsonaro at 47.0% against Lula's 45.2%. GS sees an October Fed hike as unlikely and expects the FOMC to eventually decide no further hikes are needed, and separately estimates higher rates subtract only 0.2% from 2027 GDP. For Q3, consensus S&P EPS growth is 27%, over half from AI infrastructure spending and 116% hyperscaler capex growth, though the median stock slows to 9% from 14% in Q2 and the top 10 stocks' earnings growth share rises to 68% from 48%. GS raises TSMC's 2027E revenue growth to 36.9% from 32% on AI accelerator and server CPU demand, lifts 2026 US data center capacity 5GW to 64GW and trims 2027 by 5GW to 90GW on limited political impact. In Europe, positive EPS momentum and a FCF yield gap support overweight calls on tech, banks and defense names.
